---
title: "Ship a pack in a Claude plugin"
---

A Claude plugin can carry a capt-hook pack so its hooks load in every project the
plugin is enabled for, without that project running `capt-hook init` or editing
`packs.toml`. There are two sanctioned tiers. Pick by whether the pack should
track the *repo* or track the *session*.

## Repo-scoped: `packs.toml`

This is the cc-notes model. The pack is pinned in the project's committed
`.claude/hooks/packs.toml`, so every clone hydrates the same commit and the
wiring lives in the repo. Use it when the pack encodes that repo's own
conventions.

```bash
uvx capt-hook pack add github:acme/notes@v1.2
```

`pack add` resolves the ref, caches the commit, and writes a pinned entry;
teammates run `pack update` to hydrate it. The full workflow is in
[Use packs](packs.qmd). Nothing else on this page applies to this tier — the
plugin does no per-session work.

## Session-attached: four artifacts

This is the cc-context model. The plugin ships the pack inside itself and
attaches it once per session, so it applies to whatever project the plugin is
enabled in and leaves no trace in the repo. The captain-hook plugin is the sole
dispatcher — its own `hooks.json` registers every event — so your plugin never
wires a `capt-hook run` command. It ships exactly four artifacts.

### Scaffold them

`pack scaffold` writes all four, plus a starter hook, and lints the result:

```bash
uvx capt-hook pack scaffold .
```

Pass the plugin root — the directory the attach line targets. In an empty repo
it creates every artifact; in a partial one it repairs in place, adding only
the missing contract pieces. It never touches content it can't account for: a
conforming file stays byte-for-byte identical, an unparseable one is reported
and left alone, and a hook command it can't classify stops the run before any
write. A legacy consumer built before the attach-only contract migrates in one
pass — scaffold strips the mirrored `capt-hook run` entries and leaves the
single canonical attach. It closes by printing the two-line install snippet for
your README.

The rest of this section is the contract scaffold writes and `pack lint`
enforces — read on to hand-author, or to understand what scaffold produced.

**1. The pack manifest, `capt-hook.toml`.** Unchanged from any other pack;
[Author a pack](packs.qmd#author-a-pack) covers it.

**2. One attach hook in the plugin's `hooks/hooks.json`.**

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "SessionStart": [
      {
        "hooks": [
          { "type": "command", "command": "uvx --isolated capt-hook pack attach \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}\"" }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The argument is the pack root: the directory holding `capt-hook.toml`. Pass
`"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks"` when the manifest lives in a `hooks/` subtree.
This is the plugin's only capt-hook entry; hooks that have nothing to do with
capt-hook coexist alongside it freely.

`pack attach` reads the SessionStart JSON from stdin and records the pack — its
manifest directory and version — under that session. In steady state it writes
nothing to stdout, since SessionStart stdout is injected into the model
context; the one exception is the first session on a machine that hasn't
registered a dependency marketplace yet, where attach self-bootstraps it and
prints a single notice line (see [Tell users how to
install](#tell-users-how-to-install)). A missing or invalid manifest exits
non-zero with a stderr message, so a broken plugin fails loud at author time
rather than silently loading nothing. The attach covers the whole session: a
subagent's hook events carry the same session id, so attached packs load for
sidechains too.

**3. The dependency in `plugin.json`.**

```json
{
  "dependencies": [
    { "name": "captain-hook", "marketplace": "captain-hook", "version": ">=9.9.0" }
  ]
}
```

The object form is required: `name`, `marketplace`, and a version floor. A
bare `"captain-hook"` string, or an object missing the floor, fails
`pack lint`. Floor at the oldest release your pack works with; `>=9.9.0` is
the first that ships the attach-only contract.

**4. The allowlist in your marketplace's `marketplace.json`.**

```json
{
  "allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn": ["captain-hook"]
}
```

::: {.callout-warning title="The allowlist is load-bearing"}
Without this line, Claude Code skips a `plugin.json`-declared cross-marketplace
dependency at install — no error, no captain-hook. Verified on Claude Code
2.1.207. The pack then attaches into a session where no dispatcher runs, and
every hook stays dark.
:::

## Extra dependency marketplaces

captain-hook registers itself. If your plugin depends on *other*
cross-marketplace plugins too, list their `owner/repo` slugs in your
`capt-hook.toml`, and attach registers those as well:

```toml
marketplaces = ["yasyf/cc-present"]
```

Each slug is a plain `owner/repo` (no `github:` prefix). On the first session
that finds one unregistered, the same background worker that bootstraps
captain-hook also runs `claude plugin marketplace add` for it; Claude Code then
resolves the matching `plugin.json` dependency and installs the plugin. This is
what keeps a plugin with two or three cross-marketplace dependencies at a
**one-line** install — the user adds only your marketplace, and the rest
register themselves.

Declare each extra in all three places: `marketplaces` here so attach registers
the marketplace, a `dependencies` entry in `plugin.json` so Claude Code installs
the plugin, and its name in the `marketplace.json` allowlist so the
cross-marketplace dependency is permitted. A slug that isn't a well-formed
`owner/repo` fails `pack lint` (it can't load the manifest).

## Tell users how to install

Two lines — your marketplace and your plugin:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add your-org/your-repo
claude plugin install your-plugin@your-marketplace
```

Your dependency marketplaces install themselves. Claude Code won't add an
unknown marketplace from a `plugin.json` dependency alone, so the first session
after your plugin is enabled runs its attach hook, which registers every
dependency marketplace the pack declares — captain-hook plus anything in
`marketplaces` — in a background worker, then prints one line:

> capt-hook: registering the plugin marketplace(s) yasyf/captain-hook,
> yasyf/cc-present in the background — this plugin's hooks depend on them. Takes
> effect via Claude Code's background plugin auto-update, /reload-plugins, or the
> next session.

Once a marketplace is registered, the matching `plugin.json` dependency
resolves and Claude Code installs and enables the plugin; the hooks go live that
session on `/reload-plugins`, or the next session automatically. The bootstrap
is idempotent — already-registered marketplaces short-circuit it with a single
file read — and backs off for an hour per marketplace if `claude` isn't on
`PATH` or a registration fails. `claude plugin update` alone doesn't resolve a
dependency a newer release of your plugin adds, but the attach hook
self-bootstraps on the next session regardless, so there's no manual marketplace
step on upgrade either.

## Lint the contract

`pack lint` vets all four artifacts plus the pack itself and exits non-zero on
any failure, so CI needs one line:

```bash
uvx capt-hook pack lint .
```

Pass the plugin root — the same directory your attach line passes. The checks:

| Check | Passes when |
|---|---|
| `manifest` | `capt-hook.toml` resolves under the root you passed. |
| `hooks.json` | Exactly one capt-hook entry: the canonical SessionStart attach, and zero `capt-hook run` entries. Commands are token-parsed, not substring-matched, so a reworded prefix or a `run` buried mid-command still counts. |
| `plugin.json` | The captain-hook dependency is an object with `marketplace` and a version floor. |
| `marketplace.json` | `allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn` includes `captain-hook`. A plugin with no `marketplace.json` upward gets a warning, not a failure. |
| `load` | The pack loads at least one hook with no load errors. Zero hooks fails — a pack that loads nothing ships no working guard. |
| `session-start` | No hook subscribes `SessionStart`. The attach and the dispatcher's own SessionStart run are parallel sibling hooks with no ordering guarantee, so a pack's own SessionStart hooks are unreliable by construction. |
| `async-decision` | No hook registers `async_=True` on a decision-capable event — a background hook's verdict is discarded. Registration also raises on this at runtime. |

## Precedence

When a pack name arrives from more than one tier, the more explicit source wins.
A `packs.toml` entry beats an attached pack of the same name: a repo that pins
`acme-notes` gets that exact commit even if an enabled plugin also attaches an
`acme-notes`, and the ambient attach is dropped. A repo that wants none of an
ambient plugin's pack declines it by name, which beats every source:

```toml
[packs.acme-notes]
disabled = true
```

The disabled entry pins nothing and resolves to nothing; it only suppresses the
pack, whether that pack would have come from a builtin, a `packs.toml` source, or
an attach.

Within the attached tier, packs resolve in stable name order, so gate
arbitration does not depend on attach timing. A same-name re-attach from a
different directory replaces the prior entry — the newer attach wins, because a
plugin update relocates its versioned cache directory and the pack legitimately
re-attaches from the new path — and the rebind is logged at WARNING naming both
directories, since a genuine two-plugins-one-name clash surfaces the same way
and wants a look. An attached pack no project pins loads normally, and its
hooks join dispatch like every other pack's.
